text: Sugar has a distinct sweet taste, which is one of the five basic tastes recognized by humans. It is characterized by a pleasant, sugary flavor that stimulates sweet receptors on the tongue. The intensity of the sweetness can vary depending on the type of sugar (e.g., sucrose, fructose, glucose), but it is generally described as clean, simple, and immediately recognizable. In culinary contexts, sugar not only provides sweetness but also balances other flavors, such as acidity or bitterness, and can add texture and mouthfeel to foods and beverages.
